chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Fuzayl ibn Usman, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was saying: 'A deed is not belittled when accompanied by piety, and how can one belittle what is accepted?'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: Why is a small deed not considered insignificant in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) taught that a deed is not considered small or insignificant if it is performed with taqwa (God-consciousness/piety). Since God accepts such deeds, they cannot be belittled. This hadith, found in al-Kafi, underscores the Shia emphasis on the qualitative value of actions rooted in divine awareness, linking the Prophet's legacy to the Imams' teachings on spiritual merit.
